## About these materials

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}

Please cite these materials as: Von Grebmer Zu Wolfsthurn, S., (2026). *Where to next* [PowerPoint slides]. [LMU Open Science Center](https://www.osc.lmu.de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/wrap-up/where-to-next](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/wrap-up/where-to-next)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to **bring together** different open research topics and encourage you or your audience of open research novices to **reflect on their own open research journey** and the **next steps** after having acquired and practiced all of these open research skills. This session was designed to sort through previously acquired open research knowledge and skills, and make informed **decisions about what is most relevant** given the own individual context. The aim is to **begin the design process** for a personal **implementation plan**, that is, to think about **which open research practices** make **sense** and are **relevant** given the specific context, to think about **who can support** with the implementation,  which **obstacles** can be foreseen and how they can be **mitigated**, **how behavior is changed** in a **sustainable** manner, how **knowledge can be passed** on to others and finally, how **to obtain credit** for the efforts for more robust and credible research.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Educators** in higher education with or without familiarity with open research planning to **teach open research** to **novices**
- **Self-learners** with no or limited familiarity with open research planning to **develop and build** up on their open research skills

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;"> 
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| Foundational open research skills | Replicability, R, Git, GitHub, Zotero, Quarto, simulations ... | [Access here](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/) |
| Preparatory reading | Heise, V., Holman, C., Lo, H., Lyras, E. M., Adkins, M. C., Aquino, M. R. J., ... & Weissgerber, T. L. (2023). Ten simple rules for implementing open and reproducible research practices after attending a training course. PLOS Computational Biology, 19(1), e1010750.  | [Access here](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010750) |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you or your learners will be able to ...

- **Reflect** on their own personal (research) contexts and the relevance of different open research tools and elements
- **Reflect** on the implementation of at least three open research practices in the future
- **Discuss** obstacles and their solutions to mitigate challenges in the implementation
- **Derive** a list for important support people and resources for the implementation process
